hypothesis: PageDigest reduces measured recurring synchronization work beyond the strongest eligible metadata or HTTP freshness baseline at a common bounded-staleness policy.
population: Owned loopback static HTML fixture; 10 and 100 pages, one and three independent clients, three repetitions. No production or adoption claim.

freshness.rule: Every arm must revalidate a retained body by 60 seconds; unchanged metadata never resets that deadline. Honest changes may be detected earlier by metadata. Origin failure must produce incomplete, never a completed fresh snapshot.

primary_metric: Total observed HTTP response body plus response header bytes across all assigned cycles and clients, including audits, discovery and fallback. TLS, TCP and request headers excluded.

economic_gate.secondary_guard: Report requests and publisher generation/serving CPU plus consumer CPU separately. A byte win alone does not establish dollar or lifetime cost savings.

correctness_gate: No body reused beyond the common deadline, no cross-variant reuse, complete exact resource inventory on completed cycles, no claimed completion when a required fetch fails. Expected within-deadline staleness is retained and reported.
publisher_measurement: Measure fixture metadata generation separately from request-serving thread CPU; do not claim production generator cost or CDN behavior.
negative_outcome: Any correctness violation, or less than 20 percent measured response-byte reduction against the best correct eligible arm, is no-go for the corresponding claim.
disclosures: Same author implements and evaluates this development experiment; not independently operated.
The existing persistent-consumer benchmark remains a separate unchanged regression. New freshness orchestration is experimental and uses the reference PageDigest planner.
Input specification is frozen before implementation and measurements; code hashes are retained with each run.
